correctness.rationale: For the full ten-line boundary, the Petersen incidence graph is connected and triangle-free, and intersecting geometric lines have intersection number one. The normalization sequence, with rational components, gives the connected Picard torus with character lattice the rank-six integral cycle group, including reversal signs. Independently reconstructed integral cycles by solving the edge boundary equations using the stated tree: the rooted tree minor is unimodular, all seven supplied coordinate transforms have determinant ±1, and their actual edge chains transform by the seven claimed signed blocks. Induced permutation lattices, the quadratic sign lattice, and induction of that sign from the quadratic base give the specified Weil restrictions and norm-one factors. Surjectivity of the finite-field norms and cyclicity of finite-field units give each rational-point group for every q, not only sample q. The all-field realization of the types uses the degree-five twist classification.
residual_risks: The computation certifies the integral lattice identifications, not the general twist and normalization theorems. The conclusion concerns only the full ten-curve boundary and its connected Picard torus.

evidence: The matched Resultary Finding gives the integral and finite-group tables, and includes boundary and open-complement zeta functions. Algorithms for Del Pezzo Surfaces of Degree 5 p. 1 describes S5 configuration symmetry and classifies forms by conjugate line actions; The Wiman-Edge pencil and the Wiman curve pp. 3, 7 identifies the ten-line Petersen configuration.

claim_vs_prior_implication.reasoning: The older isogeny does not identify integral restrictions. The distinct November 22 result directly identifies all seven, and the rational-point group claims then also follow; no residual torus row is established as distinct.
